Extract the reusable scene/runtime into PortfolioSaver.Presentation.
Extract the reusable settings experience into PortfolioSaver.Settings.
Keep the legacy screensaver host during Beta 5.5 for compatibility while documenting the desktop app as the primary product surface.

validated_flows: queued remote desktop UX cycle with command acknowledgement and live summary updates
ssh_first_vm_harness.interactive_launch_method: Push-VmWorkspace.ps1 stages the repo and publish bundle, Guest-ConfigureDesktopAutomation.ps1 prepares the desktop account, the host starts PortfolioSaver.VmAgent.exe in session 1 with PsExec, waits for agent-status.json, then queues a UX command JSON under commands\ that the agent executes inside the interactive desktop session while supervising WinAppDriver and invoking fullscreen through the ViewFullScreenMenuItem automation hook.
harness_policy_notes: The current SSH/SFTP plus PortfolioSaver.VmAgent desktop-session harness is the canonical supported workflow.
Do not re-optimize or re-architect the working harness glue during normal feature work.
Change the harness only when the current path is broken or a concrete new validation requirement cannot be met with the existing flow.

current_operational_recommendations: Use the SSH/SFTP remote harness for normal Windows target build, publish, and UX validation work.
Treat PortfolioSaver.Desktop as the primary runtime target for Beta 5.5 work.
Retain the legacy screensaver host only while compatibility still matters.
Use the safe-temp build/publish scripts for repeatable validation rather than ad-hoc repo-path publish commands.
Treat the remote target as a generic Windows machine so the same harness can move from a VM to a physical PC without orchestration changes.
Let PortfolioSaver.VmAgent own interactive-session automation instead of attempting to launch UX runs directly through SSH-driven PowerShell.
Use build/vm/test-secrets.json for remote live validation secrets instead of persisting any API keys into plaintext settings.json.
Treat the current agent-based remote harness glue as locked unless it breaks or a new validation requirement forces a targeted change.

current_priority_backlog.title: Use the Updated line for initial-value loading feedback instead of the large waiting overlay
evidence: User requested replacing the startup announcement-style hold overlay with a flashing top-left Updated-line message.
notes: At startup, the third status-band line should flash 'Loading initial values' until enough fresh quotes are available.
Once the initial recovery threshold is reached, the normal Updated age text should replace the loading message.
The goal is to preserve the scene presentation while making startup recovery feedback smaller and less intrusive than the current announcement-style hold state.
Resolved by removing the recovery-path waiting overlay while network is available and using the status-band Updated line as the loading indicator instead.

ScreensaverSceneControl now flashes Loading initial values on the third status-band line while StartupCoordinator.ShouldShowInitialValueLoadingStatus remains true, then automatically falls back to the normal Updated age once enough fresh quotes are present.

current_priority_backlog.title: Replace scrolling news ticker with telegraph-style item playback
evidence: User requested a telegraph/teleprinter-like news presentation instead of continuous scrolling.
notes: Render news in uppercase Courier-style typography.
Type characters in one by one for each item.
If an item is too long, advance it across the band item-by-item instead of using the current marquee behavior.
Terminate items in teleprinter style with STOP where appropriate.
After each item, pause briefly, clear the band, then begin the next item.
Resolved by replacing the marquee-loop NewsFlasherControl with a teleprinter playback state machine and by removing the upstream headline-expansion logic so only real items are played.
The band now types each item in uppercase Courier text, scrolls only when the fully typed line exceeds the viewport, pauses, clears, and advances to the next item.
Validated with focused news/render/config regression coverage plus the canonical 20-minute VM proof build/vm/artifacts/ssh-runs/ux-deep-ssh-20260515-180853.

current_priority_backlog.title: Drive the Updated time from the last S&P 500 refresh in Global Markets

notes: Use the S&P 500 item in Global Markets as the freshness anchor for the top-left Updated line.
The displayed Updated age should track the last refresh timestamp for that S&P 500 payload rather than a broader scene-level or provider-level fallback timestamp.
If the S&P 500 value is unavailable, define a clear fallback behavior during implementation.

Fallback behavior is the newest available quote timestamp when ^SPX is unavailable.
Validated with focused regression coverage plus the canonical 20-minute VM proof build/vm/artifacts/ssh-runs/ux-deep-ssh-20260515-164439.

current_priority_backlog.title: Investigate stale or inaccurate S&P 500 values in Global Markets
evidence: User observed the app showing S&P 500 at -0.60% while the actual market value was approximately -0.89%.
notes: Investigate whether the S&P 500 feed, scheduler, cache, symbol mapping, market-hours handling, or display-layer freshness rules are causing stale or lagging values.
The specific concern is that even after an apparent refresh, the S&P 500 value in Global Markets may still not reflect the latest market reading.
This ticket is about data correctness, not just timestamp labeling.
Resolved by routing ^SPX through the Yahoo Finance v8 spark/chart path instead of the dedicated quote endpoint path that was lagging or failing for this symbol.
StartupCoordinator now keeps ^SPX out of the Stooq world-index lane and reserves it for the dedicated Yahoo pass, while YahooFinanceQuoteProvider explicitly avoids the quote endpoint for ^SPX.

Verified in the canonical VM harness proof build/vm/artifacts/ssh-runs/ux-deep-ssh-20260515-160454 where trace lines show ProviderReturnedQuotes / provider=Yahoo Finance v8 / requested_symbols=[^SPX] / fetched_symbols=[^SPX] and world_index_missing_symbols=[].

current_priority_backlog.title: Constrain window sizing and formalize restored, maximized, and fullscreen behaviors
evidence: User requested a fixed minimum usable window size, a controlled restored size, standard maximized windowed behavior, and reliable true fullscreen behavior.
notes: Compute the minimum usable application window size that avoids distortion or cutoff.
Use that computed size as the fixed restored window size rather than allowing arbitrary user resizing.
Maximized windowed mode should use the normal work area outside the Windows taskbar, keeping the menu bar and full window chrome visible.
View -> Full Screen should occupy the entire screen, with F11 toggling fullscreen and Esc exiting back to windowed mode.
In restored and maximized windowed modes, the menu bar and window frame must remain completely visible.

Resolved by enforcing a fixed 1180x720 restored size, constraining maximized windowed mode to SystemParameters.WorkArea, and suppressing resize/state constraint callbacks while fullscreen transitions clear work-area caps and reapply virtual-screen bounds after the style switch settles.

Validated with focused DesktopShellMigrationTests and VmHarnessScriptTests, a full 242 / 242 local test pass, and the canonical 20-minute VM proof build/vm/artifacts/ssh-runs/ux-deep-ssh-20260515-194351 where ConfigPhaseStatus=Completed, DesktopPhaseStatus=Completed, DesktopVersionCheck=Passed, and FullScreenToggleStatus=Completed.

notes: The chosen fix was to preserve the mixed historical red and green segments while re-drawing only the latest segment on top using the current quote direction color.

HistoricalGraphBuilder now seeds a dedicated LatestSegmentPoints overlay, ScreensaverSceneControl updates LatestSegmentBrush from the live quote direction, and FloatingGraphControl renders that last-segment overlay above the historical segments.
Validated with focused ScreensaverRenderBehaviorTests covering both the dedicated overlay binding and ApplyQuoteToGraph alignment of LatestSegmentBrush with the current quote direction.

current_priority_backlog.title: Extract a clean service-ready data engine boundary between retrieval/orchestration and UI rendering
evidence: User requested a major refactor to cleanly separate data retrieval from UI rendering so the architecture can later support a Windows service and more controlled provider parallelism.
notes: Manual code-review validation summary: the core diagnosis remains correct, but the ticket must explicitly account for three seams that are easy to underestimate. First, StartupCoordinator is not just long; it directly constructs concrete infrastructure such as QuoteCacheService, multiple provider implementations, ProviderHealthService, FinanceNewsService, ScreensaverSettingsService, SymbolProfileStore, and ExchangePhotoCacheService. Second, settings, secrets, traces, and caches are still user-profile rooted through PathHelper and ProviderSecretStoreService, which means a future service-ready engine needs explicit settings/secrets abstractions rather than assuming those concerns can stay ambient. Third, several orchestration types still live under the PortfolioSaver.Screensaver.Services namespace even though the product is desktop-first, so namespace and composition cleanup should be treated as part of the refactor rather than deferred as mere polish.

Current diagnosis: the repository already has a meaningful provider layer under src/PortfolioSaver.Data and domain models under src/PortfolioSaver.Core, but the main runtime orchestration still lives in src/PortfolioSaver.Presentation/Services/StartupCoordinator.cs. StartupCoordinator is approximately 1800 lines and currently owns quote scheduling, provider fallback ordering, startup warmup policy, graph warmup, news refresh orchestration, cache usage, freshness logic, tracing, and scene-shaping decisions. ScreensaverSceneControl is over 2100 lines and still depends on some of that orchestration behavior directly. FinanceNewsService and ScreensaverSettingsService also sit in the same runtime namespace, reinforcing that the retrieval/runtime layer is not yet cleanly separated from the product surface.

The goal of this ticket is not merely to prepare for a future Windows service. The deeper goal is to establish a stable architectural seam that improves concurrency, testability, startup behavior, scheduling clarity, and future maintainability while keeping the existing desktop product working throughout the migration.

Target architecture: keep PortfolioSaver.Core for immutable models, enums, validation rules, and provider policy definitions; keep PortfolioSaver.Data for raw provider clients, caches, symbol metadata, and persistence helpers; introduce a new middle layer such as PortfolioSaver.DataEngine for quote scheduling, provider execution planning, budget/rate-limit enforcement, snapshot aggregation, startup/warmup policy, historical warmup coordination, and news scheduling; leave PortfolioSaver.Presentation focused on view-model shaping, animation, scene-state rendering, and UX display policy. Introduce explicit abstractions for settings access, secret resolution, cache paths, trace sinks, and clock/network probes so the engine is not tied directly to user-profile helpers or UI-era service classes. A future PortfolioSaver.DataService host may run the same DataEngine later, but the refactor should not depend on introducing a Windows service immediately.

Non-goal: do not attempt a big-bang rewrite, do not re-architect the locked VM harness in the process, and do not start by adding arbitrary multithreading. Parallel provider execution should be a controlled outcome of the new engine boundary, not the first step.

Phase 0 - dependency audit and boundary contracts: before moving logic, catalog every concrete dependency currently new'ed inside StartupCoordinator and related runtime services, then introduce abstractions for settings access, secret resolution, cache/storage access, trace logging, network availability, time, and provider factories. Acceptance: DataEngine can be composed from contracts rather than constructing environment-bound helpers internally.

Phase 1 - seam definition: define engine-facing contracts for quote snapshots, quote-refresh requests/results, provider execution plans, freshness anchors, startup readiness, and historical/news work items. During this phase, copy as little behavior as possible; prefer extracting interfaces and pure helper types first. Acceptance: Presentation can depend on an engine contract instead of directly owning provider ladder decisions.

Phase 2 - extract scheduler and provider orchestration: move refresh-window building, due-symbol selection, stagger logic, provider plan ordering, rate-limit cooldown handling, partial-result handling, and quote-merge logic out of StartupCoordinator into DataEngine services. Keep concurrency behavior semantically equivalent at first. Acceptance: unit tests can validate scheduling and provider fallback behavior without constructing WPF controls or scene state.

Phase 3 - extract startup/warmup and freshness policies: move initial stale-data recovery logic, dedicated Yahoo warmup rules, graph warmup coordination, startup readiness thresholds, and status freshness anchor calculation into the engine layer. Acceptance: the engine can produce a clean startup state model such as loading, warming, live, partial, stale without the scene control owning the logic directly.

Phase 4 - extract news orchestration and runtime settings access: move summarized news scheduling, feed selection cadence, cache decisions, and teleprinter item preparation into engine-facing services while keeping the visual teleprinter playback itself in Presentation. At the same time, split settings read/write concerns from runtime settings consumption so the engine depends on a read model rather than the settings UI service classes directly. Acceptance: news retrieval and news rendering become distinct responsibilities and the engine is no longer coupled to ScreensaverSettingsService.

Phase 5 - scene adaptation and namespace cleanup: reduce StartupCoordinator to a thin adapter that asks DataEngine for a state snapshot and maps that into ScreensaverSceneState and view models. Rename or relocate residual runtime classes out of PortfolioSaver.Screensaver.Services where appropriate so the desktop-first architecture is reflected clearly. Acceptance: StartupCoordinator becomes a compositional facade instead of the core runtime brain, and service names/namespaces no longer imply legacy ownership of the modern runtime layer.

Phase 6 - optional controlled concurrency: once the engine owns scheduling, add bounded async worker lanes by concern or provider group, for example Yahoo quotes, provider fallbacks, historical warmup, news, and treasury/macros. Use bounded concurrency, explicit cooldown/budget gates, deterministic merge rules, and structured tracing. Acceptance: parallelism improves cadence without introducing nondeterministic UI regressions.

Phase 7 - future service host feasibility review: only after the in-process DataEngine is stable should we evaluate adding a PortfolioSaver.DataService Windows service host. That later review must explicitly address secrets ownership, per-user versus machine-wide settings, IPC contract choice such as named pipes or gRPC over named pipes, installer behavior, and support burden. This ticket does not require implementing the service host itself.

Key risks to manage: duplicated logic during migration, freshness regressions, cache/secrets path confusion, over-eager concurrency creating race conditions, over-coupling the engine to user-profile storage, and accidental coupling back from Presentation into the engine. Mitigations: move one concern at a time, keep trace semantics stable, add regression tests before each extraction, and insist on small commits that preserve the canonical VM proof path.

Required regression coverage during the refactor: scheduling tests, provider fallback tests, stale/fresh classification tests, startup readiness tests, news cadence tests, graph warmup tests, settings/secrets abstraction tests, and at each major phase a canonical VM proof through the locked harness. No phase should be considered complete if local tests are green but the canonical VM path is broken.

Definition of done for the full ticket: a new engine layer exists; StartupCoordinator is dramatically reduced and no longer owns most provider orchestration logic; Presentation consumes engine snapshots rather than managing retrieval policy directly; provider scheduling is testable without WPF; settings and secret access are abstracted cleanly enough that a later service host would not require another deep untangling; the canonical VM harness remains the validation baseline; and the resulting architecture is ready for a later optional Windows service host without forcing another major refactor.
Deferred from the current beta lane to the next major release so the refactor can be planned and executed as a deliberate architecture program rather than mixed into current stabilization work.
Not a beta-blocker for the current lane as long as the existing locked harness and data/UI behavior remain stable enough for ongoing product fixes.

current_priority_backlog.title: Investigate reference drift for core ETF values during otherwise healthy retrieval passes
evidence: The sampled DisplayedVsReferenceFeed comparisons report drift for VOO, IJH, and IJR while other sampled symbols remain close.
notes: At least one latest sampled comparison showed VOO, IJH, and IJR materially off versus the reference feed while VEA, VWO, VSS, EFV, and EFG were close.
This must be investigated as either a true displayed-value freshness bug, a provider-source inconsistency, or a reference-comparison timing/source mismatch.

This ticket remains open because the earlier 2026-05-15 trace/reference bundle showed real drift for VOO, IJH, and IJR, but the later canonical smoke run on 2026-05-18 produced exact matches for the sampled ETF set.

Before closing it, we still need a repeatable explanation: either prove the earlier drift came from the comparison timing/source path, or capture a fresh failing case that ties the displayed drift to a real retrieval or scene-state bug.

Recommended revisit path: run a longer canonical soak, preserve both the circular trace and reference comparison artifacts, and compare whether the same ETFs drift again under live market movement rather than only in a short smoke window.

current_priority_backlog.title: Provider label still reports Live+Cache even when stale_quote_count has fallen to zero
notes: Later ApplySceneStateComplete events show stale_quote_count=0 while provider_text still renders Provider: Live+Cache.
This appears to be a status-label semantics issue rather than a retrieval failure, but it makes the runtime telemetry less truthful than it could be.
Resolved on 2026-05-18 by collapsing the top-band provider text from Live+Cache to Live once all current quotes are beyond the stale threshold. Focused render validation passed 45 / 45.
